Note::TexAccessor::ops¶

Back to Note TeX Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

TokenBatch Note::TexAccessor::ops() const

Extract Mathematical Operator Lexemes¶

ops() selects the ASCII operators + - * / = < > ^ and the TeX operator commands \times, \cdot, \pm, \mp, \leq, \geq, \neq, and \approx from complete math regions. Command tokens retain their leading backslash, making a TeX command distinguishable from an ASCII character.

This is lexical inventory rather than precedence analysis. Unary and binary minus are the same token, repeated operators remain repeated, and the method does not build an expression tree. Commands outside the explicit vocabulary are omitted even if a document defines them as operators. Use symbols() when all control words should join the operator stream.

Prose and malformed math regions are ignored. Results follow source order across each cell and carry lane ownership in offsets(). Undefined input propagates; Bool, Int64, and Float64 inputs are rejected.

Example 1: ASCII And TeX Operators¶

const auto source = pluss::make_note(
    std::vector<std::string>{
        R"(prose 99; $x_1 + \sin(\alpha) = 2.5$)",
        R"(\[\beta \leq y^2\] and \(\sqrt{z}\))",
        R"(escaped \$7 and plain theta)",
        R"($$\argmax_x f(x) \approx 10$$)"},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{2, 2});
const auto result = source.tex().ops();
std::cout << result.tokens() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[5], dim=1, numel=5, encoding=utf8)
["+", "=", "\\leq", "^", "\\approx"]

Example 2: Prose Operators Do Not Count¶

const auto offsets = result.offsets().integers();
for (auto value : offsets) std::cout << value << ' ';
std::cout << '\n';

Output¶

0 2 4 4 5

The repeated 4 confirms that the third cell’s escaped dollar and prose contributed no math operator.

Example 3: Undefined And Invalid Dtypes¶

std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << pluss::Note::undefined().tex().ops().tokens().defined() << '\n';
try {
  (void)pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::int64_t>{1}).tex().ops();
} catch (const pluss::Error&) { std::cout << "operators Int64: rejected\n"; }

Output¶

false
operators Int64: rejected

See Also¶

  • symbols: include every TeX control word as well as operators.

  • nums: extract number lexemes without their signs.

  • pm_signs: rewrite paired-sign commands instead of extracting them.
